source.title: An Information Budget for Label-Noise Memorization, and What Statistical Complexity Tracks: A Study with Multilayer Perceptrons
source.authors: C. NancyBaygorrea; Martins Gomes Otávio da Fonseca

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including results, tables, discussion, conclusion and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests related questions about fitting corrupted labels, held-out performance, optimizer variants and measured prediction properties using its own MLP experiments. It does not directly reproduce the claim versions’ random-label generalization, width sweep, architecture comparison, optimizer generalization comparison, batch-size comparison, dropout comparison, or sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own outcomes that bear on the listed versions: test accuracy under complete incorrect-label corruption; comparisons across optimizer/training variants; and the measured complexity, confidence and memorization timing properties. The paper's background citations and theoretical identities are not empirical result rows. No result tests magnitude-aware sharpness or example-removal effects.
record.test_reason: The study tests V1's chance-level held-out accuracy component using fixed, input-independent random labels on an MNIST MLP, alongside clean-label training. Complete incorrect-class corruption is a different task. The optimizer timing and stopping-rule comparisons do not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's complementary-label conclusion is accurate but incomplete. The authors also conclude that memorization information largely tracked what training accuracies implied, with chance correction recovering much of its advantage over raw memorized fraction. Mean complexity preceded memorization at low noise, coincided with confidence growth and memorization at high noise, and was comparatively weak for early stopping at high noise and corruption detection. They restrict all conclusions to one MLP architecture, two small datasets and synthetic noise.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains one MLP on synthetic corrupted labels and studies information and statistical-complexity measures; it does not reproduce the original generalization interventions or measurements. It uses Adam as its main protocol and exploratory SGD/Adam variants.
record.method_sensitivity: Corruption mechanism changes test accuracy and retained true-class information. Corruption rate changes the timing of complexity peaks; pair-flip noise places peaks in the first two epochs. The complexity peak is sensitive to temperature scaling, and optimizer/training variants change several reported timing and interpolation outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Complete UI corruption yielded 0.5% MNIST and 1.6% Fashion-MNIST accuracy; MNIST predictions retained normalized true-class information of 0.040, versus 0.002 under SU/PERM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Complementary-label corruption can retain learnable class information and is not interchangeable with input-independent random labels.

fits_no_version.finding: Complexity peak timing increased with UI corruption across optimizer variants, but remained at epoch 1 or 2 under pair-flip noise.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relationship between complexity peak timing and corruption rate depends on the noise mechanism.

fits_no_version.finding: Extending Adam training increased complementary-label fitting without reaching interpolation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite training duration affects the degree of complementary-label fitting under constant-rate Adam.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean-label test accuracy declined with UI corruption and subsequently declined during memorization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fitting synthetic corrupted labels can accompany deterioration in clean-label generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean complexity peaked before memorization at low corruption and near a confidence crossing during memorization at high corruption; variance peaks fell inside a broad memorization window.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction-complexity timing depends on confidence dynamics and corruption rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean prediction complexity separated noisy from clean SGD runs after interpolation, with remaining training-time confounding.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prediction complexity can retain information about training-label corruption after interpolation within a finite training horizon.

fits_no_version.finding: Time-averaged complexity detected corruption less well than simple label-free scores and ranked in the wrong direction at high corruption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Time-averaged prediction complexity is a condition-dependent corruption-detection score.

record.problems: Only one MLP architecture and two small image datasets were studied, with synthetic class-conditional noise. Main protocol did not interpolate any corrupted run. Extensions were exploratory. Ten runs per condition; bootstrap intervals may undercover and are descriptive. Noise seed was tied to initialization seed in the main grid. Several hypothesis criteria were lenient or difficult by construction. Some extension outcomes, especially post-interpolation comparisons, remain confounded by training time.
record.rows_left_out: None; retained 18 rows. Exact training accuracies, memorized fractions and information-budget values were not added where they do not bear on a tested version or distinct unlisted finding beyond the rows summarized.

untested.parts: Nearly perfect random-label fitting was not established: SU and PERM memorized fractions were only 0.86 and 0.88 after 200 epochs. The original architectures and datasets were not tested.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the interpolation width.
No matched comparison of absolute held-out performance under optimizer tuning. Table 13 compares losses relative to each run's own best epoch, which cannot establish optimizer performance rankings.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness or ranking of generalization gaps.
No counterfactual memorization estimates, targeted example removal or retraining comparison.

missing.what: Natural-label baseline: final clean test accuracy 0.985 (standard deviation 0.001), using the same architecture and main recipe. This supplies the natural-label side of V1's comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its SU/PERM results bear directly on part of V1, despite incomplete random-label fitting. UI results warrant no limits_scope verdict on V1 because that corruption mechanism preserves class information. Random-label fitting fractions are explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out; their omission is therefore not listed as missing.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports complete UI corruption with incorrect labels and SU/PERM comparisons, but does not train on fixed random labels and compare natural-label generalization with random-label test accuracy in the specified architectures.

The extension compares SGD and Adam variants on noisy-label training outcomes, but does not compare adaptive and SGD held-out performance under the version's limited-tuning image and language benchmark conditions.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with every label replaced by a uniformly drawn incorrect class (UI noise, ρ = 1).
rows.note: The authors report that predictions retained information about the true class despite below-chance test accuracy; this does not test the natural-label versus random-label generalization comparison specified by V1.
rows.check: UI labels exclude the true class and therefore retain class information. Below-chance accuracy on this complementary-label task does not challenge V1's input-independent random-label result.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with symmetric uniform labels (SU) at complete corruption.
rows.note: SU randomly resamples from all classes, so some observed labels may equal the true class.
rows.check: The reported 10.1% accuracy matches V1's chance-level prediction under random labels; the effect is observed, not absent. This row alone does not establish nearly perfect training fit.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Trained on MNIST with labels permuted among selected samples (PERM) at complete corruption.
rows.note: The paper compares the two input-independent label mechanisms with UI noise.
rows.check: The reported 10.1% accuracy matches V1's chance-level prediction under permuted labels; the effect is observed, not absent. This row alone does not establish nearly perfect training fit.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Compared SGD with momentum to the Adam protocol on MNIST UI-noise settings; reports the peak-time trend for mean statistical complexity.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between peak epoch of mean complexity and corruption rate
rows.note: This is a complexity peak timing statistic, not held-out performance relative to SGD or Adam, so it cannot show the optimizer-generalization comparison named by V4.
rows.check: Complexity peak timing does not measure comparative optimizer generalization.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam with a cosine learning-rate schedule to the Adam protocol on MNIST UI-noise settings; reports the peak-time trend for mean statistical complexity.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between peak epoch of mean complexity and corruption rate
rows.note: The reported statistic does not measure held-out optimizer performance.
rows.check: Complexity peak timing does not measure comparative optimizer generalization.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Compared Adam with weight decay to the Adam protocol on MNIST UI-noise settings; reports the peak-time trend for mean statistical complexity.
rows.measure: Spearman correlation between peak epoch of mean complexity and corruption rate
rows.note: The reported statistic does not measure held-out optimizer performance.
rows.check: Complexity peak timing does not measure comparative optimizer generalization or dropout effects.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Extended Adam training to 400 epochs at UI corruption rates ρ ∈ {0.8, 1}; reports memorized fraction and information at the final epoch.
rows.measure: Memorized fraction M at final epoch
rows.note: The article says the longer runs did not reach interpolation; these label-fitting numbers do not measure relative held-out optimizer performance.
rows.check: Longer Adam training on complementary labels measures neither input-independent random-label fitting nor Adam-versus-SGD held-out performance.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized signal information in test predictions after training with complete corruption.

conditions.value: every training label is an incorrect class

rows.measure: Normalized information about the true class in test predictions, ιsig
rows.note: This is a measured property of predictions under incorrect-label training, not test accuracy on the random-label task.
rows.check: True-class mutual information under complementary labels is distinct from V1's accuracy comparison.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized signal information in test predictions after complete SU corruption.
rows.measure: Normalized information about the true class in test predictions, ιsig
rows.note: This is the comparison condition for the true-class information retained under UI corruption.
rows.check: Mutual information is not the held-out accuracy named by V1.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured normalized signal information in test predictions after complete PERM corruption.
rows.measure: Normalized information about the true class in test predictions, ιsig
rows.note: The paper groups SU and PERM as the two mechanisms that produce labels independently of inputs.
rows.check: Mutual information is not the held-out accuracy named by V1.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured clean-label test accuracy on Fashion-MNIST after complete UI corruption.
rows.note: Reported as an extension; true-class information under this condition is not stated.
rows.check: Complete UI corruption supplies complementary labels, not input-independent random labels.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured best test epoch under UI noise for the main Adam protocol across corruption rates.
rows.measure: Best test accuracy against clean labels
rows.note: The paper reports Adam outcomes only here; these figures do not compare matched SGD outcomes or test the adaptive-versus-SGD generalization claim.
rows.check: The values are final test accuracies, not best test accuracies. Table 6 gives best accuracies of 0.973, 0.965, 0.948 and 0.863, with standard deviations 0.001, 0.002, 0.002 and 0.007. Neither series provides an SGD comparator for V4.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured when the mean statistical complexity peak occurs relative to memorization timing under UI noise.
rows.measure: Peak timing of mean complexity versus memorization onset
rows.baseline: Memorization onset t10 based on κ: 11–12 epochs
rows.value: Peak at median epochs 4 and 6.5 across runs; before onset
rows.note: The claim versions do not cover the timing of statistical complexity relative to label-noise memorization.
rows.check: Complexity timing tests no listed version. The reported medians concern corruption rates 0.2 and 0.4; the condition should exclude zero corruption.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean training confidence and mean statistical-complexity peak timing under high UI corruption.
rows.measure: Mean training confidence at complexity peak and distance from confidence 0.6 crossing
rows.value: Confidence averaged between 0.58 and 0.61; median peak-to-crossing distances of 1.5 epochs at ρ = 0.6 and 1 epoch at ρ = 0.8
rows.uncertainty: individual run confidence values ranged from 0.51 to 0.64 when SU and PERM at ρ = 1 were included
rows.note: The authors say the design cannot separate the timing associated with confidence from memorization at high corruption.
rows.check: Confidence at a complexity peak tests no listed version.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured the peak of within-group complexity variance relative to the memorization phase under UI noise.
rows.measure: Fraction of runs where peak of V falls within [t10, t90]
rows.note: The authors qualify this because the memorization window was wide, ranging from 10 to 72 epochs.
rows.check: Complexity-variance timing tests no listed version.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean complexity peak times under pair-flip noise in the exploratory extension.
rows.baseline: UI peak time increases with corruption rate
rows.value: Epoch 1 at every rate on MNIST; epochs 1 and 2 on Fashion-MNIST
rows.note: The text says the peak's correlation with corruption rate was weak under pair-flip noise.
rows.check: Pair-flip complexity timing tests no listed version.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Measured whether training-set mean complexity distinguishes noisy from clean runs after interpolation.
rows.measure: Run-level AUROC of mean training complexity for distinguishing ρ = 0 and ρ > 0
rows.note: Training-time confounding remains: clean SGD runs interpolated at median epoch 18, noisy runs at median epochs 113–122.
rows.check: Prediction complexity is not magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, and this comparison does not rank generalization gaps.

rows.subject: 784 - 512 - 512 - 10 multilayer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Used time-averaged per-sample complexity as a score for detecting corrupted training samples under UI noise.
rows.measure: AUROC for corrupted-sample detection, direction fixed in advance
rows.baseline: Best label-free score using the same predictions: 0.969 at ρ = 0.2; 0.659 at ρ = 0.8
rows.uncertainty: standard deviations at most 0.014 in Table 12
rows.note: This detects corrupted training examples rather than removing examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
rows.check: Corruption detection does not test removing counterfactually memorized examples and retraining. The original reversed state also conflates above-chance detection at low corruption with below-chance detection at high corruption.

relationships.condition: MNIST MLP trained for 200 epochs with complete SU or PERM corruption
relationships.reason: R2 and R3 report 10.1% clean-label test accuracy, matching the 10% chance prediction for input-independent random labels; this supports that component only.
relationships.display_finding: Both corruption methods yielded 10.1% clean-label test accuracy against 10% chance, while memorized fractions reached only 86% and 88%.

reader_labels.reason: Incorrect-class UI labels yielded below-chance test accuracy while SU/PERM yielded chance accuracy, and UI predictions retained more true-class information (R1–R3, R8–R10); this differs from the version's natural-label/random-label comparison.

reader_labels.reason: Test accuracy was 1.6%, far below 10% chance, but the paper does not give the corresponding true-class information or a natural-label condition here (R11).
